query: For a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy exposed to simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain the accelerated coupled degradation and why it occurs? Specify a controlled comparison capable of distinguishing the proposed explanation, predict the changes in total degradation and the individual wear and corrosion responses relative to a matched baseline, define the relevant boundary conditions, identify supporting evidence, and give a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) exposed to simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature, the accelerated coupled degradation is primarily due to synergistic disruption of protective oxide films by mechanical wear, which exposes fresh alloy surfaces to corrosive attack and enhances localized corrosion rates. This mechanism leads to greater total degradation than the sum of wear and corrosion acting independently.
generation.material_initial_state: Multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy with intact microstructure and native oxide film.
generation.intervention: Simultaneous application of mechanical wear (e.g., sliding) and corrosive environment (e.g., molten salt or humid air) at elevated temperature.
generation.conditions: Elevated temperature (e.g., >400°C), presence of corrosive medium, mechanical wear (sliding or abrasion), alloy in as-cast or homogenized state.
generation.structural_mediator: Protective oxide film formed on alloy surface; multi-phase microstructure with eutectic regions.
generation.mechanism: Mechanical wear disrupts the protective oxide film, exposing fresh alloy surfaces. The newly exposed surfaces are more susceptible to rapid corrosion due to the absence of passivation. Corrosion products may further weaken the surface, increasing wear rates. The interaction is synergistic, resulting in accelerated degradation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Total degradation (material loss) under simultaneous wear and corrosion will be significantly greater than the sum of degradation from wear-only and corrosion-only conditions. Both wear rate and corrosion rate will increase relative to their independent baselines.
generation.baseline: Matched EHEA samples exposed to wear-only and corrosion-only at the same temperature and environment, but not simultaneously.
generation.boundary: Hypothesis applies to multi-phase EHEAs with protective oxide films, under conditions where oxide formation is possible and both wear and corrosion are active. Not applicable if oxide films are absent or if either wear or corrosion is negligible.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of synergistic effect depends on alloy composition, oxide film stability, and environmental severity; exact quantitative increase is uncertain without experimental data.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three sets of EHEA samples: (1) exposed to wear-only, (2) exposed to corrosion-only, (3) exposed to simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature. Measure material loss (mass loss or volume loss), wear rate, and corrosion rate for each set.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the total degradation under simultaneous wear and corrosion is not significantly greater than the sum of degradation from wear-only and corrosion-only conditions, or if oxide film disruption is not observed, the hypothesis is falsified.
